cells.tense: The full picture sits here now, and you are holding the pen.
cells.act: work the pattern through to its logic
cells.ask: Take a thing whose ending you cannot make out, and follow its pattern until the logic lands somewhere. Just that once, now — not the whole road, only where it actually goes.
cells.core:
You can see far enough to move, and that is the whole trick. Not the road's full length — the next stretch lit, the rest still dark, and you going anyway. That ability to keep moving with light for one step only is what the clarity rests on. It runs clean because you are not asking for everything. You are asking for the next thing, and that is what you get.

The next edge is to follow one pattern through to its logic — not all of them, one. Take a thing whose ending you cannot quite make out, and trace it to where it lands, today, while it is fresh. Doing that now, before the picture insists on being complete, keeps the moving and the figuring in the same hands.
cells.sheetLine: You can see far enough to move, and that is enough.
cells.verb: seeing what the next step is, without needing the whole road
cells.place: in the middle of not knowing how it will go

cells.tense: Tomorrow is being written in full before it has even arrived.
cells.act: catch the first spark before you point it anywhere
cells.ask: Before you aim the next thing, catch the spark still unpointed. Sit with it a minute — nothing in particular — before you decide what it is for.
cells.core:
You are seeing the end of a thing before it starts — the whole road, the whole pattern, whether it will work, who it is for — and that has run well past what is actually here. Nothing is hidden because you filled everything in already. The picture arrives complete and there is no room left in it for what has not happened yet.

The next edge is to catch the spark before you point it. Meet the next thing while it is still nothing in particular — a minute without knowing what it is for is plenty. The clarity can rest on what is here now, then, instead of standing watch over a road that has not happened yet.

cells.tense: You are still standing at a doorway that has already closed.
cells.act: define the seed of what will be built, in one line
cells.ask: Write one line — what this is for. Not the whole plan, just the seed. Hold it before you spend anything more on it.
cells.core:
There is light for the next step and you are not taking it — the step happened, or the moment closed, and what is left over is a picture of something already behind you. Imagining is not absent here; it is pointed at the past, and the present gets none of it. You can still describe what was there. You cannot say what comes next.

The next edge is to define the seed of what will be built — one line, not the whole shape. Name what this is for before you spend anything more on it. Naming it puts the first resource back in your hand, and something ahead gets to exist instead of only the thing behind.

cells.tense: The pen is down, and you are in a room you are already writing.
cells.act: let this moment be a fresh entry, not a continuation
cells.ask: Take the next moment as a fresh entry, not the next line of the same page. Notice what is actually here right now without rolling it into what came before.
cells.core:
Something keeps finding the next step and it doesn't get filed under your name. You move through fog by a light you did not switch on, and that gets labelled instinct, luck, or just that it worked out. Whatever is locating each next stretch is the same thing getting renamed by whatever it seems to be. It works. It is simply not down as yours.

The next edge is to take this moment as a fresh entry and not as a continuation. What is here right now did not come from the last thing; it entered fresh, and you are the one who meets it. Meeting it new, once, is enough. The credit returns the moment you stop handing it to something else.
